facets.label: Reason
facets.value: The quote's tightly structured if-then logic — precisely the kind of argument an analytical, autistic-profile mind finds compelling — directly names the trap a security-first, high-neuroticism, perfectionist thinker is most likely to fall into: paralysing caution that constitutes failure by a different name. Having just relocated (a demonstrably non-cautious act) and currently feeling frustrated, the paradox lands with force: excessive caution is not the safe path it appears to be. The quote offers no comfort, only a precise reframing, which is exactly what an expert-level, high-skepticism mindset requires.

facets.label: Decision subject label
facets.value: “It is impossible to live without failing at something, unless you live so cautiously that you might as well not have lived at all - in which case, you fail by default.”
